Definition: prey, i.e. flocks devoured by animals
BiblicalUsage: In the Bible, ṭᵉrêphâh means prey taken by wild animals. In Genesis 31:39, That which was torn of beasts I brought not unto thee, and it appears again in Exodus 22:13.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe prey taken by wild animals still tells the truth about God, and I take it as it stands.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
